brief: For North Macedonia's central-state buyers, procurement intelligence is dual-published: every contracting authority must post plans, notices and awards to the central ESJN portal (e-nabavki.gov.mk, run by the Bureau for Public Procurement inside the Ministry of Finance), while several also maintain their own richer sections — Customs and the Ministry of Finance in particular expose full tender dossiers and annual plans as PDFs on their own domains, and MoF additionally runs CFCD for all EU/IPA tenders. The Health Insurance Fund and the Pension Fund are the heaviest banking/payment counterparties but publish less on-site: FZO behind a WAF, PIOM with no dedicated procurement page, so ESJN plus FOI via ASPI is the practical route for them. The State Audit Office is the strongest indirect source, naming actual suppliers, contract values and procurement irregularities for exactly these institutions. Main frictions are technical rather than legal: everything is public information, but finance.gov.mk and fzo.org.mk refused plain HTTP fetches and ESJN is a stateful ASP.NET app, so collection needs MK-locale headless browsing.
